origin.description: Slides a fixed-width window over each string in x, scores every window against each pattern, and returns the best location, distance, and matching substring.
origin.usage: afind(x, pattern, window = NULL, value = TRUE, method = c("osa", "lv", "dl", "hamming", "lcs", "qgram", "cosine", "running_cosine", "jaccard", "jw", "soundex"), useBytes = FALSE, weight = c(d = 1, i = 1, s = 1, t = 1), q = 1, p = 0, bt = 0, nthread = getOption("sd_num_thread"))

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: Strings to search in. Converted with as.character.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Strings to find (not regular expressions).

arguments.name: window
arguments.text: Width of the moving window. Omitted means nchar(pattern) for each pattern.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: When true, include a matrix of the best matching substrings.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: Distance method, including running_cosine for a fast cosine scan. A unique prefix is accepted.

arguments.name: useBytes
arguments.text: Compare UTF-8 bytes instead of characters.

arguments.name: weight
arguments.text: Edit weights for osa, dl, lv, or jw, positive and not above 1.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: q-gram size for qgram, cosine, running_cosine, and jaccard.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Jaro-Winkler prefix factor from 0 to 0.25 when method is jw.

arguments.name: bt
arguments.text: Winkler boost threshold for jw when p is positive.

arguments.name: nthread
arguments.text: Maximum threads. Checked and unused in the translation.

origin.details: Matching is case-sensitive. Both arguments are converted to UTF-8 unless useBytes is true. Parallelization is over x in R. grab, grabl, and extract are wrappers and are not this export.
origin.value: A list with location and distance matrices, each with length(x) rows and length(pattern) columns, and optionally a match matrix of the same shape.
origin.example: texts <- c("When I grow up, I want to be", "one of the harvesters of the sea", "I think before my days are gone", "I want to be a fisherman"); patterns <- c("fish", "gone", "to be"); afind(texts, patterns, method = "running_cosine", q = 3)

translation.description: Slides a fixed-width window over each string in x, scores every window against each pattern, and returns the best location, distance, and matching substring.
translation.usage: afind(x, pattern, window=None, value=True, method=None, useBytes=False, weight=(1, 1, 1, 1), q=1, p=0, bt=0, nthread=1)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: String or list of strings to search in. None is a missing string.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: String or list of patterns to find.

arguments.name: window
arguments.text: Window width. Omitted means len(pattern) for each pattern, or byte length when useBytes is true.

arguments.name: value
arguments.text: When true, include the best matching substring matrix.

arguments.name: method
arguments.text: osa, lv, dl, hamming, lcs, qgram, cosine, running_cosine, jaccard, jw, or soundex. Omitted means osa.

arguments.name: useBytes
arguments.text: Compare UTF-8 bytes instead of Unicode code points.

arguments.name: weight
arguments.text: Edit weights for osa, dl, lv, or jw.

arguments.name: q
arguments.text: q-gram size for qgram, cosine, running_cosine, and jaccard.

arguments.name: p
arguments.text: Jaro-Winkler prefix factor when method is jw.

arguments.name: bt
arguments.text: Winkler boost threshold for jw.

arguments.name: nthread
arguments.text: Checked and unused.

translation.details: None in x or pattern makes that matrix element missing. An empty x returns an empty list. running_cosine uses the same scores as cosine.
translation.value: A dict with location and distance as row-major lists of lists, and optionally match with the same shape.
translation.example: afind(["When I grow up, I want to be", "one of the harvesters of the sea", "I think before my days are gone", "I want to be a fisherman"], ["fish", "gone", "to be"], method="running_cosine", q=3)
